blindAnswers.reasoning: Last bullet specifies nearly rigid links connected by joints permitting neighboring-link relative motion. Select o1; a single rigid body and disconnected bodies omit the chain, while obligatory changing link length contradicts nearly rigid links.
The source explicitly includes position, velocity, acceleration and higher derivatives, and geometric/time-based properties. Select o1; force causation is excluded from kinematics, not acceleration.

The direct problem is described as acceleration in terms of supplied torque, followed by displacement. Select o1. Reversing desired motion to effort is the inverse problem; torque is not displacement and inverse kinematics is not a force law.

The first trajectory bullet requires a trajectory for each joint from A to B, and the raster shows theta1,theta2,theta3 for two arm poses. Select o1; an endpoint or initial angles alone do not specify joint trajectories, and a fixed torque does not replace them.

First three bullets distinguish some trajectory-executing actuators from most force/torque actuators needing effort computation. o1 reproduces this qualified introductory claim. Other options confuse trajectory and effort units or remove trajectory/dynamics.
